definition: Locating text regions in natural images — signs, labels, storefronts — as the first stage of scene text recognition (OCR in the wild).
details: Locating text regions in natural images — signs, labels, storefronts — as the first stage of scene text recognition (OCR in the wild).

explainer.lead: Scene text detection locates text regions in natural images such as signs and storefronts, the first stage before recognition. It matters because recognition fails if the text boxes are wrong.

tiers.eli5: It's like circling every bit of writing you can see in a photo of a street before reading it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run it as a detector producing bounding boxes or polygons that are cropped and passed to a recognizer; a pitfall is arbitrary orientation and perspective, so axis-aligned boxes clip rotated text.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it maps an image to a set of text regions with geometry (boxes or polygons) and confidence scores. Limits: dense, curved, or low-contrast text yields missed or merged regions.

explainer.example: A photo of a shopfront yields boxes around the store name and a price sign, which are then cropped for reading.
